keys.accounting_disclaimer: This guide is for informational purposes only and is not to be considered tax advice. For tax advice specific to your situation, please consult a qualified accountant.
keys.accounting_hero_subtitle: Accepting Bitcoin at your business doesn't have to complicate your accounting. Here's the short version — plus the tools and pros to make it painless.
keys.accounting_intro_c1: If you already accept cash or card, adding Bitcoin to your business books is simpler than it looks. You have two paths: auto-convert every Bitcoin payment to dollars the moment it arrives (no new accounting needed), or keep some as Bitcoin (a few extra numbers to track).
keys.accounting_intro_c2: This guide walks you through both — so you can pick the one that fits your business and start accepting Bitcoin with confidence.
keys.accounting_s1: The easy path: auto-convert to dollars
keys.accounting_s1_c1: The simplest way to accept Bitcoin is with a hybrid wallet that automatically sells 100% of the Bitcoin you receive for dollars (or your local currency) the instant a payment comes in.
keys.accounting_s1_c2: With this setup, your books look exactly like they do today — the final number is in dollars, every time. No cost basis, no capital gains, no new spreadsheets.
keys.accounting_s2: If you keep some Bitcoin: tracking your cost basis
keys.accounting_s2_c1: Some businesses choose to keep a portion of the Bitcoin they receive instead of auto-converting it all. If that's you, the main extra step is tracking your cost basis — the dollar value of each Bitcoin payment on the day you received it.
keys.accounting_s2_c2: Even if you think of your business entirely in Bitcoin, most tax authorities still want the dollar value reported. The good news: it's just two numbers per transaction — the amount of Bitcoin received and its dollar value on that day.
keys.accounting_s2_c3: Use the tools below to automate the lookup so you don't have to check prices every day.
keys.accounting_s3: Spending or selling the Bitcoin you've kept
keys.accounting_s3_c1: If you auto-convert every payment to dollars, skip this section — it doesn't apply to you.
keys.accounting_s3_c2: If you've kept some Bitcoin and later decide to spend or sell it, add the sale price to the same cost-basis spreadsheet. The difference between what the Bitcoin was worth when you received it and what it's worth when you spend or sell it is a capital gain or loss.
keys.accounting_s3_c6: That's it. The underlying math is identical to how any other appreciating or depreciating asset is accounted for.

keys.accounting_s4_c1: If you'd rather hand this off — or your Bitcoin accounting is more complex than a hybrid wallet can handle — we highly recommend Satoshi Pacioli Accounting Services, a firm that specializes in Bitcoin accounting for businesses.

keys.why_biz_s1: Lower fees, more for the business
keys.why_biz_s1_c1: Bitcoin payments skip the banks and credit card companies that take 2–3% from every sale. The business keeps more of what you pay — which often means better prices and better service for you.
keys.why_biz_s2_c1: Bitcoin payments settle in seconds, directly from your wallet to the business. There's no waiting days for a bank to release funds, and no costly chargeback disputes — so the business can focus on serving customers instead of fighting fraud.
keys.why_biz_s3: Free to accept, open to everyone
keys.why_biz_s3_c1: There are no contracts, monthly fees, or setup costs for a business to accept Bitcoin. And millions of Bitcoin users around the world actively seek out merchants that accept it — giving this business free exposure to new customers.

keys.why_good_for_you: Why Bitcoin is great for you too
keys.why_good_for_you_intro: Bitcoin isn't just useful at the cash register — it's a better form of money that protects your savings, your privacy, and your freedom to transact. Here's a quick overview.
keys.why_hero_subtitle: You just scanned a Bitcoin Accepted Here sticker. Here's why that's great news — for this business, and for you.
keys.why_intro_c1: The business you're at accepts Bitcoin — a modern, open-source payment network that anyone can use, anywhere in the world, without banks or middlemen taking a cut.
keys.why_intro_c2: Below is the short version of why accepting Bitcoin is good for this business, plus why using Bitcoin is good for you as a customer.
keys.why_s1_c1: Inflation happens when more money is printed or created from thin air. That makes the money in your pocket worth less over time — and it's why prices keep going up year after year.
keys.why_s1_c2: Bitcoin has a fixed supply of 21 million coins. No government, bank, or company can print more of it. Your Bitcoin savings hold their value over time instead of quietly losing it.
keys.why_s2_c1: Multiple U.S. banks have collapsed in recent years because of bank runs. When too many customers tried to withdraw at once, the banks didn't have the cash to pay everyone back.
keys.why_s2_c2: Instead of just holding your money, banks lend and invest most of it. If those investments go bad — or if depositors lose confidence — the bank can fail, and your deposits can be frozen or lost.
keys.why_s2_c3: With Bitcoin, you can hold your own money directly in your own wallet. No bank. No intermediary. No bank run.
keys.why_s3_c1: Unlike credit cards, PayPal, or traditional bank accounts, Bitcoin doesn't require anyone's permission to use.
keys.why_s3_c2: No one can freeze your account, block a payment, or cut you off from the network. It's the first financial system in history you can use freely, without fear of censorship or seizure.
keys.why_s4: Bitcoin is building a better world
keys.why_s4_c1: Bitcoin is often misunderstood, but it's quietly doing a lot of good in the world.
keys.why_s4_c2: It has helped human rights activists fight for freedom, reduced global methane emissions from landfills and oil fields, stabilized electric grids, and funded public goods like national parks.

keys.inflation_aud_btc_p1: Inflation means your money buys you less over time. Bitcoin is better money because it doesn't have inflation.
keys.inflation_aud_btc_p2_after: because it has a maximum supply of 21 million Bitcoin. No one can print more Bitcoin.
keys.inflation_aud_btc_p2_before: Dollars have an unlimited supply, which means more can be printed at any time.
keys.inflation_aud_btc_p3: Historically, Bitcoin has gained purchasing power over time while the dollar has lost it. Many people use Bitcoin as their long-term savings account: money that they can leave alone and let grow for several years.
keys.inflation_aud_btc_p4: Would you rather save in dollars that buy you less over time? Or save in Bitcoin that has historically bought you more over time?
keys.inflation_aud_freedom_h2: Bitcoin is also a tool for freedom

keys.lightning_s1_c1: Lightning enables you to send Bitcoin payments quickly and cheaply.
keys.lightning_s1_c2: It's important to know that using lightning comes with trade-offs. In exchange for faster, cheaper Bitcoin payments, you often sacrifice some security.
keys.lightning_s1_c3: In general, Lightning should only be used with small amounts of bitcoin. You should only ever store large amounts of bitcoin in a hardware wallet.

keys.lightning_s2_c1: One of the innovations of Bitcoin is the ability to store it without relying on a custodian, like a bank. Self-custody wallets unlock the full power of Bitcoin.
keys.lightning_s2_c2: With a self-custody wallet, you are the only one with the ability to spend or transfer your money. No one can stop you, censor you, or steal from you when you use a self-custody wallet. These are also called non-custodial wallets.
keys.lightning_s2_c3: The most sovereign way to use Lightning is by running your own node.
keys.lightning_s2_c4: This guide is focused on simple Lightning wallets that don't require your own node.
keys.lightning_s2_c5: It's important to know that even using a non-custodial Lightning wallet, you are still trusting the wallet creator not to push a malicious app update and steal your funds.
keys.lightning_s3_c1: Custodial wallets are wallets where you are not in control of your money.
keys.lightning_s3_c2: These wallets are more similar to the banking system where you must trust a third party to give you access to your money. If your Bitcoin is on an exchange, you are using a custodial wallet.
keys.lightning_s3_c3: Custodial wallets can seem convenient, but the custodian has the technical ability to steal all user funds at any time.
keys.lightning_s3_c4: Some people prefer custodial Lightning wallets for small amounts of bitcoin because of their ease of use. Just remember: not your keys, not your coins!

keys.wallets_question_3: How will I back up my recovery phrase?
keys.wallets_s1_c1: Bitcoin wallets are interoperable, so you can send Bitcoin to anyone no matter which wallet they use.
keys.wallets_s1_c2: There are many different Bitcoin wallets that differ in important ways. You can determine if a wallet is right for you by asking these simple questions:
keys.wallets_s2_c1: One of the innovations of Bitcoin is the ability to store it without relying on a custodian, like a bank.
keys.wallets_s2_c2: If you're holding bitcoin on an exchange or in an ETF, you lose the freedom benefits of bitcoin.
keys.wallets_s2_c3: Self-custody wallets unlock the full power of Bitcoin: freedom money.
keys.wallets_s2_c4: With a self-custody wallet, you are the only one with the ability to spend or transfer your money. No one can stop you from sending or receiving your money when you use a self-custody wallet.
keys.wallets_s2_c5: Self-custody wallets are also called non-custodial wallets.
keys.wallets_s3_c1: Custodial wallets are wallets where you are not in control of your money.
keys.wallets_s3_c2: These wallets are more similar to the banking system where you must trust a third party to give you access to your money. If your Bitcoin is on an exchange, you are using a custodial wallet.
keys.wallets_s3_c3: If you bought a Bitcoin ETF, you are using a custodial wallet that doesn't allow you to withdraw to self-custody.
keys.wallets_s3_c4: Custodial wallets can seem convenient, but the custodian has the technical ability to steal all user funds at any time.
keys.wallets_s3_c5: Not your keys, not your coins!
keys.wallets_s4_c1: Cold wallets store the keys to your Bitcoin in a manner that never exposes them to the internet.
keys.wallets_s4_c2: This significantly limits the attack vectors that a thief might use to try to steal your Bitcoin, and is best used for large sums of Bitcoin that you don't need to transfer often.
keys.wallets_s4_c3: You can think of a cold wallet as a long term savings account, also known as cold storage.
keys.wallets_s5_c1: Hot wallets store the keys to your Bitcoin on a device that is connected to the internet, like your phone.
keys.wallets_s5_c2: Hot wallets are generally considered safe, but they could have more security vulnerabilities than cold wallets.
keys.wallets_s5_c3: You can think of a hot wallet like you would a physical wallet. You wouldn't store your entire savings in your wallet, but you would store some spending money.
keys.wallets_s5_c4: Hot wallets make it much easier to spend your Bitcoin without having to pull your entire savings out of cold storage.
keys.wallets_s6_c1: When you set up your Bitcoin wallet, your device will generate a recovery phrase. This recovery phrase (also called a seed phrase) contains 12 or 24 words.
keys.wallets_s6_c2: If you ever lose access to your wallet or your device stops working, you can input this recovery phrase into a new wallet to regain access to your Bitcoin.
keys.wallets_s6_c3: Most wallets include a sheet of paper to write down your recovery phrase, but lots of people prefer to back up this phrase on steel instead. This makes it much less likely to lose your recovery phrase in the event of a natural disaster like a fire or a flood.
keys.wallets_s6_c4: Jameson Lopp has tested 70 steel backup kits to help you pick the one that is right for you.
keys.wallets_s6_c5: View Jameson's metal Bitcoin backup guide here.
